Showing how a Minion of Tyranny was terribly punished for interfering with the conservative Women of America. And describing the Kentucky Chap's remarkable Skirmish with his Thanksgiving Dinner. arxiv-2007-11714.title: Interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya Interaction of Antiferromagnetic Materials
arxiv-2007-11714.creator: Md. Rakibul Karim Akanda, In Jun Park, Roger K. Lake
arxiv-2007-11714.description: Abstract The interface between a ferromagnet (FM) or antiferromagnet (AFM) and a heavy metal (HM) results in an antisymmetric exchange interaction known as the interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (iDMI) which favors non-collinear spin configurations. The iDMI is responsible for stabilizing noncollinear spin textures such as skyrmions in materials with bulk inversion symmetry.

arxiv-2106-02314.title: Isomers in 203 Tl and core excitations built on a five-nucleon-hole structure
arxiv-2106-02314.creator: V. Bothe, S.K. Tandel, S.G. Wahid, P.C. Srivastava, Bharti Bhoy, P. Chowdhury, R.V.F. Janssens, F.G. Kondev, M.P. Carpenter, T. Lauritsen, D. Seweryniak, S. Zhu
arxiv-2106-02314.description: Abstract Isomers with three- and five-nucleon-hole configurations have been established in 203 Tl. These include newly identified levels with a three-nucleon structure: I π = (15/2 - ) with T 1/2 = 7.9(5) ns, and I π = (35/2 - ) with T 1/2 = 4.0(5) ns.

arxiv-2108-04530.title: Suppression of crosstalk in superconducting qubits using dynamical decoupling
arxiv-2108-04530.creator: Vinay Tripathi, Huo Chen, Mostafa Khezri, Ka-Wa Yip, E. M. Levenson-Falk, Daniel A. Lidar
arxiv-2108-04530.description: Abstract Currently available superconducting quantum processors with interconnected transmon qubits are noisy and prone to various errors. The errors can be attributed to sources such as open quantum system effects and spurious inter-qubit couplings (crosstalk). The Z ​ Z ZZ -coupling between qubits in fixed frequency transmon architectures is always present and contributes to both coherent and incoherent crosstalk errors.

arxiv-2201-13330.title: Gradient estimate for complex Monge-Ampere equation with continuous right hand side
arxiv-2201-13330.creator: Xiuxiong Chen, Jingrui Cheng
arxiv-2201-13330.description: Abstract . In this note, we consider complex Monge-Ampere equation posed on a compact Kähler manifold. We show how to get L p L^{p} ( p < ∞ p<\infty ) and L ∞ L^{\infty} estimate for the gradient of the solution in terms of the continuity of the right hand side. 1.

The attempt to prove Corollary 6.13 naturally led to the study of the 𝖲𝖧𝖤𝖱 \mathsf{SHER} principle, already defined by Dorais and al. [ dorais2016uniform ] . Thanks t
arxiv-2206-00571.creator: Julien Cervelle, William Gaudelier, Ludovic Patey
arxiv-2206-00571.description: Abstract 𝖢𝖠𝖢 ​ 𝖿𝗈𝗋 ​ 𝗍𝗋𝖾𝖾𝗌 \mathsf{CAC\ for\ trees} is the statement asserting that any infinite subtree of ℕ < ℕ \mathbb{N}^{<\mathbb{N}} has an infinite path or an infinite antichain. In this paper, we study the computational strength of this theorem from a reverse mathematical viewpoint.

arxiv-2309-07121.title: Option pricing and hedging for regime-switching geometric Brownian motion models Thanks: Partial funding in support of this work was provided by the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada. The authors thank Hugo Lamarre for his helpful suggestions.
arxiv-2309-07121.creator: Bruno Rémillard, Sylvain Rubenthaler
arxiv-2309-07121.description: Abstract . We find the variance-optimal equivalent martingale measure when multivariate assets are modeled by a regime-switching geometric Brownian motion, and the regimes are represented by a homogeneous continuous time Markov chain. Under this new measure, the Markov chain driving the regimes is no longer homogeneous, which differs from the equivalent martingale measures usually proposed in the literature.

arxiv-2405-06617.title: Optimal Uniform Circle Formation by Asynchronous Luminous Robots
arxiv-2405-06617.creator: Caterina Feletti, Debasish Pattanayak, Gokarna Sharma
arxiv-2405-06617.description: Abstract We study the Uniform Circle Formation ( UCF ) problem for a swarm of n n autonomous mobile robots operating in Look-Compute-Move (LCM) cycles on the Euclidean plane. We assume our robots are luminous , i.e. embedded with a persistent light that can assume a color chosen from a fixed palette, and opaque , i.e.

arxiv-2505-13618.title: Spectrum of BPS black holes in A ​ d ​ S 3 × S 3 × S 3 × S 1 AdS_{3}\times S^{3}\times S^{3}\times S^{1}
arxiv-2505-13618.creator: Matthew Heydeman 1 , Xiaoyi Shi 2 , Gustavo J. Turiaci 2
arxiv-2505-13618.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Matthew Heydeman 1 , Xiaoyi Shi 2 , Gustavo J. Turiaci 2. We uncover novel features in the spectrum of BPS and near-BPS states in asymptotically A ​ d ​ S 3 × S 3 × S 3 × S 1 AdS_{3}\times S^{3}\times S^{3}\times S^{1} spacetimes. This follows from a careful analysis of semiclassical and quantum black holes in this theory, which have peculiarities due to the nonlinear large 𝒩 = 4 \mathcal{N}=4 superconformal symmetry.

arxiv-2508-04628.title: Simulations of dielectric permittivity of water by Machine Learned Potentials with long-range Coulombic interactions
arxiv-2508-04628.creator: Kehan Cai, Chunyi Zhang, Xifan Wu
arxiv-2508-04628.description: Abstract The dielectric permittivity of liquid water is a fundamental property that underlies its distinctive behaviors in numerious physical, biological, and chemical processes. Within a machine learning framework, we present a unified approach to compute the dielectric permittivity of water, systematically incorporating various electric boundary conditions.

arxiv-2601-12764.title: Relativistic Hamiltonian as an emergent structure from information geometry
arxiv-2601-12764.creator: Sikarin Yoo-Kong
arxiv-2601-12764.description: Abstract We show that the relativistic energy–momentum relation can emerge as an effective ensemble-averaged structure from a multiplicative Hamiltonian when fluctuations of an auxiliary parameter are treated using maximum entropy inference. The resulting probability distribution is uniquely fixed by scale-invariant constraints, which are shown to arise naturally from the Fisher–Rao geometry of the associated statistical manifold.

pmc-10674992.creator: You Wu, Hongyi Yu, Jianping Du, Chenglong Ge
pmc-10674992.description: In the realm of aviation, trajectory data play a crucial role in determining the target’s flight intentions and guaranteeing flight safety. However, the data collection process can be hindered by noise or signal interruptions, thus diminishing the precision of the data.

pmc-11421823.title: Evaluation of quadriceps muscle cross-sectional area using an ultrasonic diagnostic equipment with a wide field of view
pmc-11421823.creator: Yasumoto Matsui, Marie Takemura, Yasuo Suzuki, Tsuyoshi Watanabe, Keisuke Maeda, Shosuke Satake, Hidenori Arai
pmc-11421823.description: Skeletal muscle index measurement via dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry or bioelectrical impedance analysis is used to evaluate muscle mass when diagnosing sarcopenia. However, inherent challenges exist with these methods. We previously focused on muscle mass evaluation in the quadriceps femoris by using computed tomography (CT).

pmc-11551935.title: Severe Rheumatic Carditis in a High Resource Setting
pmc-11551935.creator: Jake Lesser, Heena Mansuri, Shanna Kowalsky-Herbst, Julie Kantor, Jose U. Mendoza, Ryan Halickman
pmc-11551935.description: A 6-year-old boy developed acute rheumatic fever after group A streptococcal pharyngitis. Despite prompt diagnosis and adequate treatment, he developed progressive rheumatic heart disease. Given the rarity of acute rheumatic fever in the U.S. population, timely diagnosis with echocardiographic screening and vigilant follow-up are crucial to mitigate rheumatic heart disease complications.

pmc-11691329.title: MICROBIOME ROLE IN COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT: MIAGB COHORT INSIGHTS
pmc-11691329.creator: Sidharth Mishra, Lauren Buddendorff, Julia Hoover, Rohit Shukla, Vivek Kumar, Shalini Jain, Hariom Yadav
pmc-11691329.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Aging population is increasing, leading to a rise in aging-related conditions, specifically diseases like Alzheimer’s disease and its related dementia (ADRD), which have poor prognosis and lack prevention and treatment strategies. Although we do not fully understand the complex pathology of ADRD, emerging evidence indicates that abnormalities in the gut microbiome contribute to ADRD pathology, but how this occurs remains largely unknown.

pmc-12539185.title: From glia limitans to glial scars: in vitro co-culture studies of the astrocyte and meningeal interaction
pmc-12539185.creator: Erin C. Reardon, Aisling J. Greaney, John J. E. Mulvihill
pmc-12539185.description: The brain-meninges interface, comprising of astrocytes and meningeal cells seperated by a shared basement membrane, plays critical roles in the central nervous system. Recent work has shown the importance of signalling between the brain and the meninges in neurodevelopment, health, disease, and in stem cell migration. Despite this recent research, the brain-meninges interface is significantly understudied.

pmc-12736780.title: Volume and Attenuation Characteristics of Chronic Subdural Hematoma: An Annotated Patient Cohort of 257 Patients with Interrater Reliability Assessments
pmc-12736780.creator: Mattias Drake, Emma Hall, Birgitta Ramgren, Björn M Hansen, Johan Wassélius, Zhongwei Zhang
pmc-12736780.description: Simple SummaryChronic subdural hematoma is a common condition, especially in older adults, and the accurate measurement of its size on CT scans is essential for guiding treatment decisions. In this study, we analyzed 257 patients and found that manual measurements of hematoma volume are highly reliable between different radiologists and correlate well with a simple estimation formula.

pmc-13092809.title: Quantifying setup uncertainty between computed tomography guidance and magnetic resonance guidance in intramuscular metastases radiotherapy
pmc-13092809.creator: Travis Salzillo, Surendra Prajapati, Zhiqian Henry Yu, Yao Zhao, Tze Yee Lim, He Wang, Xin A. Wang, Xinru Chen, Rajat Kudchadker, Belinda Lee, Angela Sobremonte, Ahsan S. Farooqi, Devarati Mitra, Andrew Bishop, Chad Tang, Jinzhong Yang
pmc-13092809.description: Background and purposeMR‐Linac (MRL) is well‐suited for treatment of oligometastatic disease (OMD) in muscle due to its superior soft tissue contrast. The purpose of this study was to assess dosimetric differences and quantify margins when CT‐guidance (CTgRT) is used for OMD treatment compared to MR‐guidance (MRgRT) on the MRL.

pmc-13126643.title: Tetrazolylidene-Stabilized Gold(I) Complexes: Synthesis and Evaluation of Anticancer Activity In Vitro
pmc-13126643.creator: Simon Stifel, Claudia Schmidt, Leon F. Richter, Alexander Pöthig, Angela Casini, Fritz E. Kühn
pmc-13126643.description: The first comprehensive study of a series of seven mesoionic tetrazolylidene gold­(I) chloride complexes (1–7) featuring a range of alkyl and aryl substituents (Me, t-Bu, iPr, Ph, Tol, Dipp, Mes) is reported. Three synthetic pathways enabling access to scarcely explored abnormal 1,3-disubstituted tetrazolium ligand precursors (L 1 –L 7 ) have been established.

pmc-13191986.title: Family support, stigma, and psychological detachment in hemodialysis patients: a cross-sectional mediation analysis
pmc-13191986.creator: Liu Cong, Wu Jianyi, Lyu Xiaoran, Wang Qin, Liu Nian, Li Xianglin, You Lang, Zou Li, Wei Yongting, Xi Zuyang
pmc-13191986.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundMaintenance hemodialysis (MHD) patients face profound psychological challenges that impede their quality of life and treatment outcomes. Understanding the interplay between family support, illness-related stigma, fear of progression, and psychological detachment is crucial for developing effective psychosocial interventions.AimsThis study aimed to investigate the relationships among family support, stigma, fear of disease progression (FoP), and psychological detachment in MHD patients, and to examine the mediating roles of stigma and FoP.MethodsA cross-sectional study was conducted from November 2024 to January 2025.

pmc-13256757.title: Connexin 26 in Hearing Health and Disease: StructuralFoundations, Mutation Mechanisms, and Therapeutic Perspectives
pmc-13256757.creator: Weihua Qiu, Kaelah Schneider, Youzhong Guo
pmc-13256757.description: Mutations in gap junction protein β-2 (GJB2), encoding Connexin 26 (Cx26), are the most common genetic cause of hearing loss, responsible for up to 50% of inherited non-syndromic cases worldwide. This review covers Cx26 from three perspectives: protein structure, mutant disease mechanisms, and treatment approaches.

pmc-13303640.title: One Health Perspective on the Enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli Diversity
pmc-13303640.creator: Ricardo Rodríguez-Martínez, Jetsi Mancilla-Rojano, Sara A. Ochoa, Graciela Castro-Escarpulli, Ariadnna Cruz-Córdova, Juan Xicohtencatl-Cortes
pmc-13303640.description: In this review, the virulence factors involved in enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli (ETEC) colonization and pathogenesis are analyzed, with an emphasis on colonization factors, enterotoxins and antigenic diversity as central challenges in vaccine development. ETEC remains a major cause of diarrhea worldwide, particularly in vulnerable populations.

pmc-13486332.title: Effects of exercise snacks on cardiorespiratory fitness, body composition, and blood lipids in adults across different age groups: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13486332.creator: Lidian Meng, Yichen Li, Jiayi Chen, He Zheng
pmc-13486332.description: Graphical abstract Introduction The World Health Organization has identified insufficient physical activity as an important global health risk. In 2022, approximately 31% of adults worldwide, equivalent to about 1.8 billion people, did not meet the recommended levels of physical activity.
